title: Pakistan E-commerce Price Prediction
summary: A price-prediction workflow built around Pakistani e-commerce transaction data and deployable inference.
problem: Price-prediction work needs a disciplined path from transaction data to reproducible inference.
solution: A data-science workflow evaluates tree-based approaches and packages an inference-oriented application.
architecture: Case-study context: Price-prediction work needs a disciplined path from transaction records to features, model comparison, and a repeatable inference surface.
Data preparation: Python and pandas shape the transaction data into a reproducible modeling input. Components: Python, pandas, Jupyter.
Model comparison: Scikit-learn supports tree-based experiments with Random Forest and Gradient Boosting as inspectable approaches. Components: scikit-learn, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting.
Inference surface: Flask packages the selected path into a small application boundary for prediction-oriented use. Components: Flask.
Python, pandas, and Jupyter prepare transaction data for modeling.
Scikit-learn supports tree-based experiments including Random Forest and Gradient Boosting.
A Flask application packages an inference path for price estimates.
outcomes: Deployable inference workflow translating e-commerce transaction data into price estimates.
Kept the result framed as deployable inference rather than a verified business forecast.
Omitted unverified R² and row-count figures.
